\begin{tablenotes}\notesize
\item Notes: Each cell is the coefficient of Eq.~(\ref{eq:group}) with a monthly flow of workers in place of the log count of workers: the three-year difference, per standard deviation of the stage-1 to stage-4 change in exposure, in the number of workers entering or leaving the occupation each month per 100 base-period workers of the group in the occupation, with the twelve base-period composition shares, base-period group employment weights, a period effect, and standard errors clustered by occupation in parentheses. Movers are identified by linking consecutive monthly interviews of the same respondent in the CPS rotating panel. Non-employment is unemployment plus being out of the labor force. An entrant from non-employment was unemployed or out of the labor force in the previous month, and an entrant from another occupation was employed under a different occupation code; exits are the reverse, and exits to unemployment are the part of exits to non-employment whose destination is unemployment. The last column is the change in entrants from all sources minus the change in exits to all destinations, estimated on the cells where both are observed. The monthly rate from the linked sample is multiplied by the group's employment in the occupation and quarter to obtain the count, so that quarters with no movers remain in the sample. Moves between occupation codes include coding noise: about 7 percent of linked workers employed in both months carry a different occupation code, against 2 percent among those who report the same employer, so the non-employment columns are the cleaner measure. A net coefficient of $-$0.37 in the first row cumulates over 36 months to a decline of about 13 percent, against the 8.20 log point decline in the number of workers under 30 over the same window (Table~\ref{tab:cell_fd_main_4}), but its standard error is wide. $N$ is between 502 and 899 occupation-quarter cells in Panel A and between 1,045 and 1,792 in Panel B. \textsuperscript{*} $p<0.10$, \textsuperscript{**} $p<0.05$, \textsuperscript{***} $p<0.01$.
\end{tablenotes}
